clue.text: Boxer who sat up after a clobbering

indicators.note: something clobbered is battered out of shape, so the letters before it are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A fighter is knocked down and only sits up once the beating is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed fighter, one who leads with the right hand from a left-hand stance.

clue.text: Cancel journey after a number of deliveries

indicators.note: one piece after another means it is placed later in the answer

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A trip is called off after several parcels have been dropped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post; in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, six making an over.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to cancel it by using superior authority.

clue.text: Politician who raises the roof

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Margaret ..., British prime minister 1979 to 1990
second meaning, taken literally: a craftsman who puts up straw roofs

explanation.surface: A politician who makes a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raises the roof' is an idiom for being noisy, but here it is literal: building a roof of straw or reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was Britain's longest-serving modern prime minister, and a thatcher builds roofs of reed or straw.

clue.text: Gave money to area beset by rising depression

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so the word goes backwards
beset means surrounded, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a dip is a hollow in the ground
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone hands over cash to a region hit by a deepening economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: Paid is the past tense of pay, to give someone money owed.

clue.text: Is mixing with women attractive?

indicators.note: things mixed are stirred together, so these letters combine in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether socialising with women makes one appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming in an engaging, innocent way.

clue.text: Instructions to leave a high-rise building derelict

definitions.text: Instructions to leave a high-rise building
definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: go down the stairs, then out of the door
second meaning: a destitute, homeless person

explanation.surface: A tall building being evacuated has been left to decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derelict' seems to describe the building; it is the noun for a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-and-out is a destitute person with no home or money, which is what a derelict is.

clue.text: Lose current agent destroyed after attempt that's lost billions

indicators.note: one piece after another means it is placed later in the answer
losing billions means dropping the letter that abbreviates a billion

parts.note: to have a stab is to make an attempt

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so the word just before has its letters reassembled

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A spy's failed effort costing billions wipes out his up-to-date status.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the usual abbreviation for billion. 'Current' sounds like being up to date, but it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that stagnates stops flowing, losing its current and becoming stale.

clue.text: Note tons absorbed in needlework

indicators.note: something absorbed in another is taken inside it

parts.note: crochet is needlework done with a hooked needle
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A message mentions masses of something absorbed in sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note lasting one beat, called a quarter note in America.

clue.text: A figure fancier and strangely tailored

indicators.note: done strangely means done in an odd way, so the following word's letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone who likes a good figure is also oddly well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure fancier' suggests someone admiring a shapely body; here the figure is an idol, a carved image.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships images, so is literally a lover of carved figures.

clue.text: Daughter perhaps is telling stories

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a family member, of which a daughter is one example
second meaning: the act of narrating or recounting

explanation.surface: A girl is accused of making things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling stories' hints at lying, but here it simply means recounting, as in the relation of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a kinsman such as a daughter, and also a narration or account of events.

clue.text: Ray perhaps is small and perversely heavy

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
heavy put in a contrary, roundabout way: not light

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is described as short and oddly weighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perversely' asks for heavy to be expressed back to front in sense, as the negative of its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of the sun is one example of the light that sunlight is made up of.

clue.text: What could be flyover crew's problem on the earlier road

definitions.text: What could be flyover crew's problem on the earlier road

parts.note: surface reading: the staff working on a raised modern road
setter's reading: the danger once faced by travellers on old coaching routes, a robber who manned them

explanation.surface: Workers on a modern raised road face some difficulty compared with older routes.
explanation.walkthrough: A flyover is a raised road, so its crew could be called high-way men; the real answer is the mounted robber of old roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounted robbers held up coaches on the roads of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, a hazard for any traveller.

clue.text: Account by America — time I have a word in case that's objective

definitions.text: a word in case that's objective

parts.note: ACC is the abbreviation for account
the United States of America
T is the abbreviation for time
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: An American bookkeeper takes someone aside for a quiet word about an impartial case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' reads as impartial; in grammar the objective case marks the object of a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a noun in the accusative stands as the object of a verb, the objective case.

clue.text: Ruin — it lies west of here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wreck, as hopes are wrecked
second meaning, cryptic: the punctuation mark printed in this clue sits to the left of these words

explanation.surface: Directions to a ruined building somewhere to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half refers to the clue itself: on the page, west means to the left, and the mark printed there is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to ruin them, and the long horizontal stroke in the clue is a punctuation dash.

clue.text: Southeastern battlefield's no open aspect

parts.note: the compass abbreviation
Crécy in northern France, site of the 1346 English victory

explanation.surface: A battlefield in the southeast has no open views.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrecy is the condition of keeping things hidden, the absence of any openness.

clue.text: Disdainful second refusal over British blunder

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
no is a refusal
B is the abbreviation for British
bish is British slang for a mistake

explanation.surface: A haughty second rejection is made over a British gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the earlier pieces sit before the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: A snobbish person looks down on those they think beneath them, holding them in disdain.

clue.text: Vessel's company reported over girl, we hear?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: a crew is a company of workers

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so it is the pronunciation that matters

parts.note: Sybil is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is gossiped about over some young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, which fits 'company'; it is a container for melting metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is a heat-resistant pot in which metals are melted, a container or vessel.

clue.text: Clubs undergoing trial for competition

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
something being tried out is on test

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are being trialled ahead of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a competition between rivals for a prize or victory.

clue.text: What takes its toll of fish dangling from reel?

indicators.note: in a down clue something dangling hangs below, so it comes later in the answer

parts.note: to reel is to spin or turn
the pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler's catch hangs from the reel, and something is costing someone dearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes its toll' is an idiom for doing damage; here it is literal, collecting tolls.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a road where travellers pay a toll, originally at a gate.

clue.text: Alone around home, ending in black and hard depression

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word goes round the pieces that follow

parts.note: sole means only or alone
being in means being at home

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the last letter of black
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone alone at home falls into a black, hard depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as low mood; it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinkhole is a hollow in the ground made where the surface collapses, a kind of depression.

clue.text: Wife putting on fleecy layer

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to put on is to add

explanation.surface: A wife puts on a woolly garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadding is soft fibrous padding used to line or stuff, a fluffy layer of material.

clue.text: Burden — and where it might fall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a responsibility or duty
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.surface: A weight, and the question of who ends up carrying it.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and the second half reads naturally: a burden falls on us.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility, and split into two words it says the load lands on ourselves.

clue.text: A little son being important

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
to matter is to be important

explanation.surface: A small boy thinks himself very important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little son' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount, especially a slight knowledge of something.

clue.text: Frustrated Christian's superior and unruly fellow

parts.note: Captain Bligh of the Bounty, whose first mate Fletcher Christian led the mutiny
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a rowdy 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's boss is irritated and a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a believer; it is Fletcher Christian, mutineer on HMS Bounty.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighted hopes are spoiled or thwarted ones, so the word fits frustrated plans.

clue.text: See cricket perhaps missing runs

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for the next word is dropped

parts.note: cricket is one example of a sport
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Watch the cricket, perhaps, with no runs being scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Shut up Zulu bands performing around king

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the bands go round the ruler named straight after

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors
R for rex, Latin for king
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: An order to silence Zulu musicians playing around their king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests musical groups, but these are regiments of warriors.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut someone up can mean to lock them away, which is what imprisoning does.

clue.text: Tsar following dictator killing off a popular composer

indicators.note: killing off removes something entirely, here the single letter named straight after
one piece following another means it is placed after it in the answer

parts.note: Sulla was a dictator of ancient Rome
Ivan the Terrible, first Tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler succeeds a dictator who kills off a well-liked musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Sullivan wrote the music for Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Sullivan composed tuneful light operas that made him one of the best-loved Victorian musicians.

clue.text: One harvesting fish circling at a particular point

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one word wraps around the words after it

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
there means in that particular place

explanation.surface: A fish swims round and round at one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatherer collects crops or wild food, the work of anyone bringing in a harvest.
